rules.text: Nontidal waters (MD), statewide: harvest 06-16–02-28 12 in minimum 5 per day / 10 possession, combined with largemouth
Catch-and-return areas: Potomac River from Dam No. 2 (Seneca Breaks) up to the Monocacy mouth; Monocacy River from the Potomac up to Buckeystown Dam: catch-and-release only
Maryland owns the Potomac riverbed to the low-water mark on the Virginia shore (Black-Jenkins 1877). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_v._Maryland
Do not confuse with other Tuscarora Creeks (e.g. the Monocacy tributary of the same name).
License: Maryland nontidal license (Matt's stated license; not verified here) (per Matt; not verified)

rig.primary: 3.5 in root-beer or green-pumpkin tube on a 1/4 oz internal tube jighead, 20 lb braid to 4 ft 10-12 lb fluoro
rig.alternate: 2 in shallow crankbait (crawfish) or 3.5 in paddletail on a 1/8-1/4 oz jighead, 20 lb braid to 4 ft 12 lb fluoro, #1 snap for cranks
rig.switch_trigger: Fish chasing or seen busting bait, stained water, or no bites dragging bottom in 30 min
rig.gear_note: Workable on the 7 ft Crossfire MH (20 lb braid) with the leader dropped to 10-12 lb; ideal is a 6'6"-7' medium-light/medium spinning rod with 8-10 lb braid. The unconfirmed 6'6" Ugly Stik fits with a lighter leader.

next3h|full|false.rig_line: 3/8-1/2 oz round jighead (3/0-4/0), 4-5 in white or chartreuse paddletail, 24-30 in 30 lb fluoro tied direct to 20 lb braid (FG knot)

drivers.text: incoming tide in window (species pref plus)
drivers.label: forecast

details.confidence_note: flow/tide data in hand; DNR report under 30 days mentions it; water temp measured

presence.note: MD DNR public lands page: fishing permitted for brackish water species such as rockfish, perch, and bluefish.

access.note: No parking on the DNR facility itself. Park in the Talbot County-maintained 'Black Walnut Point Fishing Area' lot a short distance away at 4787 Black Walnut Point Rd, Tilghman. Capacity conflicts: fishandhunt says the paved lot holds up to five cars; Delmarva Trails calls it 'large'; a Google review quoted by TourTalbot says 'plenty of parking'. Porta-potties. No entry fee.

rules.text: Chesapeake Bay and tidal tributaries (MD), excluding Susquehanna Flats, Lower Susquehanna River and Northeast River: harvest 05-01–05-15 19-24 in 1 per person per day; 05-16–05-31 19-24 in 1 per person per day
Striped bass, Chesapeake Bay rules: November falls inside the Sep 1 to Dec 5 harvest season (1 fish per day, 19 to 24 in). Catch-and-release only Dec 6 to 31.

The point is at the Choptank mouth, and the Choptank is a listed spawning river closed to targeting Mar 1 to May 31. Whether the point lies inside that boundary is not verified; this matters only in spring.
License: Maryland Chesapeake Bay & Coastal Sport Fishing License (Matt states he holds a MD tidal license; not verified) (per Matt; not verified)

rig.primary: 3/8-1/2 oz round jighead (3/0-4/0), 4-5 in white or chartreuse paddletail, 24-30 in 30 lb fluoro tied direct to 20 lb braid (FG knot)
rig.alternate: 4-5 in white or bone popper or walk-the-dog plug (~1/2-3/4 oz), loop knot to 24 in 30 lb fluoro
rig.switch_trigger: Low light, flat calm, fish or bait busting on top in under 10 ft of water
rig.gear_note: Fits Matt's 7 ft Daiwa Crossfire Inshore MH with 20 lb braid and 30 lb leader; he owns 1/4-3/8 oz jigheads and 4 in paddletails. Buy 1/2-3/4 oz heads for inlet/bridge current
